conflicts: Brief Alignment proposes: Retain the full title, controls, Start action, HUD, skier, gates, and trees, but reduce or lift the title card so more of the downhill route is visibly traceable behind it. Additional literal detail can increase one-off components and rough exceptions unless each addition is expressed through the established construction system. Clarity proposes: Reduce the title panel's height and lift it slightly to reveal more of the slope while preserving the title as the first read. Changing scale and contrast for hierarchy is useful, but ad hoc emphasis must not introduce unrelated borders, shadows, typography, or spacing. Expressiveness proposes: Integrate the title and start prompt into the game world's pixel HUD, add content-driven slope variety such as tracks, moguls, and one iconic hazard, and give the skier a more distinctive animation pose or trail while preserving the strict pixel language. Extra shapes, textures, glows, and differentiated treatments can fragment palette, geometry, and material logic if each becomes a bespoke exception.
accept: Accept every fidelity restoration, hierarchy correction, and thematic differentiation that can be built from shared grid, type, palette, stroke, radius, elevation, and illustration tokens. Accept stronger focal contrast and a distinctive hero treatment, but keep their construction precise and reuse their rules in related states.
compromise: Implement the craft foundation first: Choose a base pixel unit and snap all scene geometry, borders, shadows, icons, and decorative marks to multiples of it. Map every required or expressive addition onto a small documented token set, while allowing deliberate scale and color-role differences for hierarchy. Use one exceptional hero treatment at most; all supporting components must share alignment, typography, outline, lighting, and spacing rules, with clipping and viewport-edge defects resolved.
